paragraphs: Caution signals | This page corresponds to the O*NET 43-4199.00 Information and Record Clerks, All Other residual occupational group: O*NET explicitly states that the All Other title represents a group of occupations with substantial differences in characteristics that cannot be assigned to a specific O*NET-SOC occupation, and O*NET does not provide task, skill, work activity or Job Zone data for such titles. Therefore this page focuses on the occupational group's official basis (including US wages and employment) and a general information and record work process description, and does not fabricate a specific task list. The work involves the accuracy of data and records and delivery and compliance boundaries: one record error, one inconsistent data basis, one unauthorized disclosure of information can all cause delivery or compliance risk. The US wages and employment are on this occupational group's basis (median annual wage 49,500 USD; 2024 employment about 153,300, 2024—2034 growth almost no change, annual average openings about 17,800). If it is hard for you to bear repetitive record checking and accuracy pressure, treat these as real costs that need serious weighing.

Taking on judgment | True fit comes from whether you can do three things at once in the same job: do the records and data solidly (receive the task and constraints, check data and record files, carry out recording and analysis, check results, producing reviewable records and reports); keep standards and compliance under control (data accuracy, personal information and information disclosure boundaries, delivery and compliance requirements, executed per institutional and regulatory requirements); and bear a definable position responsibility (be responsible for your own records and conclusions, and request or hand over information disclosure or high-risk decisions beyond authority). It is suggested to test this with one verifiable experience (completing a completely fictional information recording and analysis task package and debriefing record), rather than relying only on the conclusions of an interest questionnaire.

To judge whether you suit other information and record clerks, first use public or simulated material for one verifiable drill: set up a completely fictional information recording scenario (for example organizing a batch of forms and records and producing a summary), and write out the step-by-step process from receiving the task and constraints, checking data and record files, carrying out recording and analysis, checking results, handling anomalies, to handing over records, marking each step's check points and possible problems (missing data or inconsistent basis, records not matching the source files, unauthorized disclosure of personal information or sensitive data, inconsistent cross-department bases, overdue delivery). When done, check: whether data accuracy, compliance and information boundaries, and the authorization and escalation path are treated as non-omittable items; whether disclosure or high-risk decisions beyond personal authority are written as requests or handovers; and whether the process is kept as a reviewable record. All material must be fictional and must not use real personal information.

Fit signals | O*NET 43-4199.00 is an All Other residual occupational group, officially described as various information and record clerks not listed separately. The general work process is: receive the task and constraints → check data and record files → carry out recording and analysis → check results → handle anomalies → hand over records. If you are willing to stably carry out recording, analysis and evidence checking around data and record files, and to hand over and escalate accurately under delivery and compliance pressure, these daily demands are closer to your way of working; interest and personality tools are used only to design exercises and cannot judge hiring qualifications or performance.

Information and Record Clerks, All Other corresponds to US O*NET/SOC 43-4199.00 Information and Record Clerks, All Other. Official note: the All Other title represents a group of occupations with substantial differences in characteristics that cannot be assigned to a specific O*NET-SOC occupation, and O*NET does not provide data for such titles. The official scope is: all information and record clerks not listed separately. Therefore this page does not fabricate a specific task list and instead focuses on the occupational group's official basis and a general information and record work process: taking data and record files as the object, receiving the task and constraints, checking data and record files, carrying out recording and analysis, checking results, handling anomalies and handing over records within delivery and compliance boundaries. The US wages and employment on this page take the precise basis of that occupational group as presented by O*NET; precise Chinese occupational wages were not obtained and are registered as a visible gap; the China-side information and personal information protection systems are marked separately.

entries: Input objects | Information and record clerks, all other take data and record files as the object and carry out recording, checking and analysis within delivery and compliance boundaries; the specific tasks depend on the institution and position concerned, and O*NET provides no task list for this All Other title.
Checkable outputs | Reviewable records and summaries, data checking results, and anomaly and handover records; results must be traceable to the source files and basis.
Complete work process | Receive the task and constraints → check data and record files → carry out recording and analysis → check results → handle anomalies → hand over records.

paragraphs: Editorial work reality check: specific positions may handle records, forms, summaries and handover, and the data source, version, access rights and delivery requirements must be checked; these are observation directions, not formal O*NET tasks or work context survey data.

Environment and pace | This occupational group includes widely differing positions, and the work environment and pace vary with institution, industry and position; it is mostly desk-based recording and checking, and delivery deadlines and compliance requirements affect work pressure.

O*NET43-4199.00 is an All Other residual group and provides no task, skill, interest, work activity or Job Zone data; BLS wages and employment can be listed separately. 2025 national pre-tax employer wages, 10/25/50/75/90 annual percentiles 33,870/40,910/49,500/59,970/71,420 USD, median hourly wage 23.80 USD. Precise SOC43-4199 information and record clerks, all other: 2025 employment 143,100, 2035 projected 144,300, growth 1%, 2025—2035 annual average openings 15,000 (including growth and replacement, not net additions or actual hiring). The main industries are government and educational services, which do not represent a Chinese statistical correspondence.

What this work checks first: the objects (data, record files and related information), the inputs (tasks and constraints, data basis, information disclosure and delivery authority, version-controlled material), and the deliverables (reviewable records and summaries, data checking results, anomaly and handover records). Any item not verified should be treated as pending verification and cannot be replaced by publicity or proxy bases. Because this page is an All Other occupational group, the specific tasks are subject to the institution and position concerned.

The work loop is judged in four steps: input check (confirm the task, data basis and authority) → task limitation (record and analyze only within the known scope) → execution and recording (complete recording and checking per standards and leave a trail) → review and escalation (stop immediately on anomalies and out-of-authority matters and report). The loop holds only if the data source, basis and authority are verifiable, not if only the final deliverable is examined.

Adjacent duty boundaries | This page covers only the occupational group O*NET/SOC 43-4199.00 Information and Record Clerks, All Other. Adjacent occupations such as interviewers (except eligibility and loan), library assistants (clerical), loan interviewers and clerks, new accounts clerks and order clerks differ in work object, authorization scope and responsibility boundaries and cannot be interchanged by job title alone, nor can proxy bases replace institutional authorization, licenses and final responsibility.

Interviewer (except eligibility and loan) direction | The core output is collecting information through interviews and completing acceptance or referral; it revolves around applicant and eligibility information. This occupational group centers on the recording, checking and analysis of data and record files; the collection method, authorization and responsibility boundaries differ and cannot be interchanged by job title alone.

Library assistant (clerical) direction | The core output is clerical and information handling around collections and reader affairs. This occupational group focuses on general data and record handling; the work objects and industry context differ, and sharing tools does not mean sharing responsibility, so the evidence must be made up separately.

Loan interviewer and clerk direction | The core output is document checking and process handling around loan applications. This occupational group focuses on general records and analysis; financial compliance and authorization boundaries are involved, responsibility differs, and the two cannot be applied to each other.

New accounts clerk direction | The core output is information collection and checking around account opening. This occupational group focuses on general data and record handling; customer identity and compliance requirements are involved, the authorization and responsibility boundaries differ, and the output and responsibility must be checked separately.
Information and record clerks, all other, work objects and the AI boundary: which steps may be assisted and which judgments must remain with people.

No measured AI adoption rate, productivity or net job impact was obtained for this residual occupational group; record organization, drafting and field anomaly alerts are editorial trial candidates and must be tested with this institution's tasks. The occupational group is internally diverse, and no uniform substitution probability is given. AI Impact Score 67% is an editorial estimate. Model impact index for three equally weighted representative core tasks; not a measured share of working time or a job-loss probability. floor((75+75+50)/3+0.5)=67; fermatmind-ai-impact-v1; 2026-10-18.The three tasks, ratings and sources are listed in the FermatMind method source record on this page.

O*NET provides the residual group definition and BLS wages and employment but no task, skill or Job Zone survey; the NIST AI RMF provides a voluntary risk governance framework and does not establish legal authorization or occupational effects; the US Department of Labor Hiring entry point is not a specific rule prohibiting model-determined delivery.

Editorial comparison: text drafting and record proofreading can be assessed for assistance, and no measured acceleration magnitude, adoption order or cross-occupation comparison was obtained. Information disclosure, changes and exception handling are checked against actual authority.

Editorial governance suggestion: clarify inputs, scope of use, review responsibility, anomalies and authority; specific legal obligations are checked separately per behavior and jurisdiction, and a general Hiring page is not used to create prohibitive rules.

First check the original records, versions and disclosure authority, then test tools in an authorized environment; there is no evidence of irreplaceability, general efficiency gains or job change causality.
Editorial trial candidates: information categorization, drafting or field anomaly alerts; the occupational effect was not verified.

Human control points: must trace back to the original data and record files and review key judgments, and bear responsibility for data accuracy, information disclosure, and delivery and compliance conclusions.

Chinese statistical tables have no single-occupation wage precisely corresponding to this occupational group; an industry average cannot be passed off as a median, and the Chinese page language does not constitute a Chinese equivalent occupation or a wage mapping.

Occupational scope | The China-side conclusions on this page are limited to the mainland China market and the current statistical basis; public statistics are published by industry category and do not distinguish occupations, and this page does not present occupational-level values.

Insufficient evidence: public Chinese occupational statistics have not established a national occupational wage distribution for information and record clerks, all other, that precisely corresponds to US O*NET/SOC 43-4199.00; the National Bureau of Statistics publishes average wages by industry category and does not distinguish occupations, and this page does not use industry averages, recruitment quotes or US data to fill in.

Interpretation note | The figures on this page are the statistical basis for an All Other occupational group and do not target a particular institution or specific position; they cannot be used as an individual quote and cannot be directly compared with mainland China or any other market.

Industry basis | The O*NET industry page shows that this occupational group's main US industries are Government and Educational Services; industry distribution, recruitment demand and annual openings are different indicators and cannot be conflated into a single growth rate.

Influencing factors | Institution type (government, education, enterprise), industry, region and position duty scope affect actual income level and stability; the percentiles on this page are statistical positions and do not correspond to specific years of experience.

As an information and record clerk, all other, which interests, abilities and work styles matter more? This page discusses fit only through work samples and responsibility boundaries and does not substitute personality labels for qualification and performance judgments.

Direct answer | The fit signals include stably carrying out recording, analysis and evidence interpretation around data and record files and handing over accurately under delivery and compliance pressure, not personality labels. Interest and personality tools can only help design exercises and cannot judge hiring qualifications, authorization or performance.

Positive signals | Able to complete recording and analysis per standards, check data and record files, check results and handle anomalies; able to keep the process and conclusions as reviewable records and hand over accurately within delivery and compliance boundaries.

Caution conditions | Risk signals include skipping checks to be fast, continuing despite an inconsistent data basis, disclosing information beyond authority, or being unwilling to escalate anomalies per authority; if it is hard to bear repetitive record checking and accuracy pressure, treat these as real costs that need serious weighing.

Trial action | Use a completely fictional information recording task package for one drill: organize data and record files, carry out recording and analysis and produce results, review points and escalation records; test with an observable deliverable rather than relying only on an interest questionnaire.
This residual group has no official RIASEC; record checking and service preferences are editorial self-questioning directions.
No validation study was obtained on the Big Five scales predicting performance in this residual group; it cannot be asserted that personality cannot predict at all.
No validity for MBTI type on occupational performance was obtained, and competence is not judged by type.

Data accuracy risk | Trigger: missing data, inconsistent basis, or records not matching source files. Consequence: may cause wrong delivery or decisions. Control: check data and record files, keep the source and version, and stop and escalate on anomalies. Boundary: final handling is determined by the applicable jurisdiction, institution and authorization chain.

Delivery risk | Trigger: overdue delivery, misunderstanding of scope, or inconsistent cross-department bases. Consequence: may affect downstream processes and compliance. Control: confirm the task and constraints, clarify the delivery scope and basis, and report promptly on anomalies. Boundary: delivery commitments beyond authority must not be made by an individual directly.

Compliance and information boundary risk | Trigger: unauthorized disclosure of personal information or sensitive data, or unclear disclosure scope and basis. Consequence: may cause compliance risk and harm to rights. Control: handle information within the minimum necessary and authorized scope, keep handling records, and decisions affecting delivery or compliance must not rely on models alone. Boundary: disclosure and high-risk decisions are made by authorized personnel per institutional rules.

Records and handover risk | Trigger: record errors, version loss of control, or incomplete handover information. Consequence: may interrupt subsequent processes or leave responsibility unclear. Control: record per standards, keep change and handover trails, and record and escalate on anomalies. Boundary: the division of responsibility is subject to institutional rules.

Common escalation rule | Once data, authorization or compliance conditions are insufficient, stop the relevant steps first and hand the facts, impact and pending questions to the responsible person with authority as a reviewable record; contracts, professional opinions or organizational authorization must not be overridden, nor may proxy bases or model output replace institutional authorization and final responsibility.

How to enter an information and record clerk, all other, position: first identify the specific position and check the announcement's education, tasks, supervision and authority; the O*NET residual group has no uniform Job Zone preparation data.

Positions in this group are heterogeneous, and no uniform education, training period or license threshold was obtained; first check the target institution's tasks and education requirements, and separately confirm position training, hiring and data authority. The education description on the OOH combined page cannot be taken as a uniform threshold for this residual group.

In the US, check education, tasks and training per the target position, and the O*NET certification or training search entry point is not a uniform required list; in China, check per the announcement, specific behavior and the information handling jurisdiction.

Qualification boundary | A course or certificate does not automatically grant this occupation's license, signature rights or high-risk authority; education, certificates, licenses, position hiring, institutional authority and signature responsibility are different states, and specific requirements depend on the position and applicable rules.
Editorial responsibility scope: understanding institutional tasks must follow the specific position and authority, and authority cannot be automatically obtained from a stage name.

Reviewable evidence | Use a completely fictional information recording task package to demonstrate ability: organize data and record files, carry out recording and analysis and produce results, review points and escalation records; do not use real personal information, and note the basis and assumptions.

Next action | Complete one fictional task package and debriefing record, ask an experienced person to challenge your checking and escalation judgments, and on that basis decide whether to keep investing in this direction; prove ability with an observable deliverable rather than a course name.

Transition path | Before transitioning, first list the transferable capabilities (recording and checking, data analysis, basis unification, compliance and information handling, record trail), then clarify the new position's tools, qualifications and responsibility evidence that must be made up; directions adjacent to this occupational group share tools but not responsibility.

description.text: What information and record clerks, all other do, how to enter and train, what risks and authorization boundaries exist, and which tasks AI will change. This page corresponds to the O*NET/SOC 43-4199.00 All Other residual occupational group, and O*NET provides no task or skill data; the official occupational group basis and US wages and employment are retained, and the mainland China wage gap is registered as evidence.

title.text: Information and record clerk, all other occupational judgment: work, entry and risk boundaries

subject.name: Information and record clerks, all other
subject.summary: Information and Record Clerks, All Other corresponds to the US O*NET/SOC 43-4199.00 Information and Record Clerks, All Other All Other residual occupational group. Official note: the All Other title represents a group of occupations with substantial differences in characteristics that cannot be assigned to a specific O*NET-SOC occupation, and O*NET does not provide data for such titles; the official scope is all information and record clerks not listed separately. This page focuses on the occupational group's official basis and a general information and record work process: taking data and record files as the object, receiving the task and constraints, checking data and record files, carrying out recording and analysis, checking results, handling anomalies and handing over records within delivery and compliance boundaries. The US wages on this page are taken from the BLS OEWS 2025 data presented by O*NET (median annual wage 49,500 USD, median hourly wage 23.80 USD), and employment and outlook are taken from the BLS employment projections 2024—2034 (about 153,300 in 2024, growth almost no change, annual average about 17,800 openings), all on that occupational group's basis; precise Chinese occupational wages were not obtained and are registered as a visible gap.
